question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?
reasoning_content:

The chunk MS-TRADE-2026-10-21-IN-01#3 mentions mass-affluent but it's a Cerulli report finding about 401(k) participants, not Morgan Stanley describing targeting mass-affluent. Also it's in "search pool" for another sub-question, but it's listed below. Hmm, but it says "Also in this sub-question's search pool (listed for another sub-question of this firm)". So it's available.

That chunk: "A June 2025 Cerulli Associates report found that 63% of active 401(k) participants do not have a financial advisor, while 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor say their retirement savings account provider is their primary source of retirement planning guidance." That's an industry figure, not MS describing. Then "The road ahead... Morgan Stanley survey arrives..." So no MS explicit statement about targeting mass-affluent.

So the answer: not_found? Or not_disclosed? Passages don't say anything about MS describing targeting mass-affluent. There are passages about channels (E*TRADE, Workplace, self-directed, digital, advisor-led) which arguably describe attracting clients through funnel — but not mass-affluent specifically. Hmm. Is that a different_quantity? No — the sub-question asks for a description, a qualitative statement. A related quantity: MS describes attracting clients via Workplace channel / E*TRADE digital / mass market funnel, but doesn't use "mass-affluent." That's arguably not_found for the specific description. But is it not_disclosed? Not_disclosed requires passages showing the firm does not report it, or report surrounding figures without it. Here there is no figure at all; the sub-question is qualitative. I'd say not_found — passages say nothing about mass-affluent targeting. Hmm, but there are adjacent statements about "20 million Wealth relationships," "top of the funnel," "self-directed households," "workplace participants" (mass market/emerging affluent). These are the closest thing — describing attracting clients across channels. Could label different_quantity with differs_because: describes broad retail/workplace/self-directed client acquisition rather than mass-affluent specifically. That seems appropriate per the instruction "When unsure between fact and different_quantity, choose different_quantity and say why."

I think best: different_quantity with items citing MS-TR-2025Q4#9 ("With 20 million Wealth relationships..."), MS-TR-2026Q3#30 (bank-first clients, top of funnel), MS-DECK-2026-strategic-update#31 (Core client relationships definition), MS-TR-2024Q4#50 (three channels: FA, E*TRADE, Workplace). And mention the Cerulli industry figure? That's an industry figure not for firm's own figure — the rules say an industry figure for a firm's own figure is different_quantity. But here the asked item is a description of targeting, so the Cerulli stat isn't a firm figure. Maybe include as item noting mass-affluent mentions in a survey context? Hmm, I'd include the Cerulli chunk as an item showing "mass-affluent" appears only as an industry survey statistic, not MS's own description. But careful: the item should state what the passage says. It's an industry figure, not about MS. I'll include it since it's the only mention of mass-affluent, and note the scope as industry survey. Actually including could risk confusion. I'll include it with scope "industry survey (Cerulli Associates)" — hmm, items for different_quantity should support the "different, related quantity". I'll include the firm-channel items primarily and maybe the Cerulli one as context. I'll include 3-4 items.
